/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 23 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2673 (-2)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4315 (-41)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1965 (-6)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1522 (38)
Baltic Handysize Index: 791 (10)
CAPESIZE
The market softened slightly today, with the BCI 182 5TC easing by $368 to $39,130. While the headline move was relatively modest, underlying sentiment weakened, particularly in the Pacific basin. Conditions in the Pacific were softer overall despite healthy volumes, with the C5 index declining by $0.255 to $12.995 and a quieter tone prevailing. Only one major was active, though underlying demand from operators remained evident. Trading activity was more measured, with bids emerging in the mid $12s against opening offers in the mid $13s, eventually settling around $12.90, with operators fixing at $13.00-$13.15 level. In the Atlantic, the tone appeared more balanced, with signs of a potential standoff or the market finding a near-term floor. The C3 index was effectively flat, easing marginally by $0.050 to $33.218, with limited activity and narrow spreads reported. The ballaster list for May loaders remains tight, offering some underlying support. On the macro side, Brent crude remains highly volatile above $100, driven by stalled US–Iran negotiations and continued disruption through the Strait of Hormuz, reinforcing concerns over prolonged supply risk.
PANAMAX
Today we experienced a mixed move between both basins. The Atlantic market continued to slip downwards with increasing tonnage off the North Continent and a weaker looking supply of grains for transatlantic trades. Mineral supply is still evident but not significant enough to switch the negative sentiment and downward market movement. With this in mind, it is of no real surprise that the P1A fell by $212 to $14,318. The P2A dropped by $289 today, despite steady grain supply from North Coast South America. Much of this volume is for forward dates which is not adding much support on the near term. US Gulf grain fronthaul activity is also softening, with bids trending lower and owners gradually adjusting their offers. In Asia, the positive sentiment has continued with the P3A marking an increase of $150 to conclude at $18,742. There have seen a number of reported fixtures from Australia, Indonesia, and the North Pacific reflecting the continued cargo flow. The P5TC posted a move downwards of $62 to $17,682.

Atlantic
The Lotus Blossom (82,616 2021) open Santos 11th May was reported to have fixed to Messrs Cofco for a trip to the Far East at around $20,000-$21,000 daily plus a ballast bonus of $1 million-$1.1 million.

Asia
Nasaka (81,837 2014) Fangcheng 24/27 April was fixed for an Indonesia to India coal run at $20,000 daily, while Aquavita Glory (81,668 2020) open Shanghai 26/30 April secured $21,000 for a North Pacific to Singapore-Japan petcoke trip with Oldendorff. Elsewhere, Vita Melody (81,671 2018) open Mariveles 1/2 May was reported fixed for an Indonesia to India coal trip at $21,000. It remains unclear across these fixtures which, if any, include scrubber benefit.
SUPRAMAX
More activity surfaced today as both the Atlantic and Asian basins gained more upward momentum. In The Atlantic, some did feel that the fronthaul demand had fallen again, but the was still interest for trans Atlantic requirements. The South Atlantic remained balanced. Brokers said that increased enquiry and limited fresh prompt position had seen a push in rates from the south for coal business. There was also a good amount of back enquiry giving owners a few options. Period cover was sort, the Langlois Skiathos (64,000 2026) a new building open ex Imabari yard was heard fixed at $22,000 for minimum 5 months / maximum 7 months trading with Drydel. Also, Opal Wealth (64,241 2025) Dongjiakou was linked to Swire's covering a vessel for 5/7 months trading at $21,000. From last week the SSI Challenger II (64,638 205) was heard basis delivery Xiamen for a minimum of 5 months / about 7 months trading at $19,750 and scrubber benefit for Owners'. The 11TC average closed up $481 at $19,241.

Atlantic
The FJ Viola (61,174 2020) open New York was heard fixed for a trip from Pascagola to Mersin at $33,000 with Pangaea. Also, the Agios Nektarios 1 (56,722 2010) open New Orleans was heard fixed on voyage terms to the Black Sea with Flame, but no more details emerged. The Seahunter (63,253 2024) (scrubber fitted) open Dublin 21/23 April was heard fixed via ECUS redelivery Continent at around $16,000 with wood pellets.

Asia
It was rumoured that an ultramax was fixed from the Philippines via Indonesia redelivery WC India at $31,000 but no more details came to light. Also, a supramax was fixed basis delivery Singapore via Indonesia redelivery India in excess of $30,000, again however no more details surfaced. Elsewhere a 61,000 was heard fixed basis delivery Soth Africa for a trip to China at $19,000 plus $190,000 ballast bonus.
HANDYSIZE
The market posted a generally positive performance, as some regions remained stable while others recorded stronger gains. The BHSI climbed 10 points to 791, and the 7TC average rose by $185 to finish at $14,235. In both the Continent and the Mediterranean, movements were limited, with rates only slightly firmer than previous levels. Although reported activity remained subdued, the South Atlantic and U.S. Gulf continued to show solid momentum, supported by very tight tonnage availability for April positions. In Asia, trading stayed active, with both owners and charterers lifting their rate ideas.

Atlantic
The Devbulk Sare (40,445 2012) was placed on subjects for a petcoke trip from Dos Bocas to Jacksonville at $17,000, fixed by Trithorn, although no further details emerged. Meanwhile, the SSI Providence (37,899 2020) was also heard placed on subjects for a grain trip from SW Pass to the Continent, fixed by Lauritzen, but the rate remained undisclosed. Similarly, the Saint Dimitros (33,788 2011) was reported on subjects for a coke trip from Barranquilla to ARAG, again by Lauritzen, with rate and additional details unknown.

Asia
The Blue Alexandra (32,545 2005), open in Penang on 28 April, was fixed for multiple laden legs at $14,000. The Darya Rapti (40,058 2022), open Singapore 29 April–2 May, was also placed on subjects for multiple legs at around $18,000, though no further details were reported. The Aurelia (37,293 2012), open Taiwan, was fixed for a backhaul trip from Korea to the US Gulf at $14,500 for the first 80 days, thereafter $17,000, by Panocean, with further details remaining undisclosed.

Market Fundamentals
West Australian Grain Under Pressure

A surging mouse plague in Western Australia, which accounts for around half of all Australian grain exports, threatens the 2025/26 growing season, newswires report. With as many 3000-4000 burrows per hectare in West Australia,farmers are fearing a full-scale plague as numbers also continue to rise in the Southern part of the country. Historically, rodents can impact yields by 5–15% in affected zones, especially during the April-May planting window. This crisis compounds existing challenges for Australian farmers, who are already struggling with shortages of fuel and fertilizer due to the Iran war. Industry estimates suggest Western Australia's grain harvest could fall ~45% from a record 27 Mt last season to around 15 Mt on insufficient fertilizer applications.

Trading Commentary
Cape
A backwards step for Cape paper, closing well in the red for the day and backed by a negative physical index print of -$368, a break in the recent run of positive prints. May started the day trading just off last night closing levels, and a series of better offers left the contract closing at $33400, with lows of $33250. Jun traded $33200 down to $32750, closing just off the lows at $33800. Q3 traded $30750 down to lows of $30500, valued at $30400 at close. Q4 traded a few times between $30400-$30300. Cal27 traded $25650 and closed at $25550, with lows of $25500.

PMX
Pmx traded flat across the whole curve in today session, may was paid at a high of 19350 and a low of 19100 closing at 19200, jun traded at a low of 19450 up to 19700 causing the jun/jul to get paid at 375. Q3 held steady bouncing around 18600 to 18800. Q4 saw participation today printing 17175 - 17250, cal 27 saw a narrow range of 14800 - 14850. Overall the pmx curve remained flat into the close.

SMX + HANDY
SMX marked was relatively flat to yesterday, trading within a similar range over the day, with liquidity largely focused to the prompt months. May traded between 18100 – 18500 and Jun 17950 – 18300 in over 2500 lots, accounting for the majority of the days cleared volume. Q3 traded within a tight range 16900 – 17000, Q4 15650 – 15800 and Cal27 traded 13200. The Handy market once again was supported, Jun trading 16200, Jul 15250, Q3 at 14800 and Q3+Q4 at 14400.

Carbon
A robust auction result pushed EUA Futures higher during the morning session, however traded volumes remain below average. Today's EU Common compliance auction settled 2.7m EUAs at �73.63, over �0.50 higher than last night's daily spot close and not far below Tuesday's auction result. As a result, the EUA Futures market traded steadily higher during the morning before levelling off in the afternoon. During the assessment window, the Dec26 contract was trading at �74.80/eua, up �0.41.

Market Fundamentals
West Australian Grain Under Pressure
A surging mouse plague in Western Australia, which
accounts for around half of all Australian grain exports,
threatens the 2025/26 growing season, newswires report.
With as many 3000-4000 burrows per hectare in West
Australia,farmers are fearing a full-scale plague as numbers
also continue to rise in the Southern part of the country.
Historically, rodents can impact yields by 5–15% in aﬀected
zones, especially during the April-May planting window. This
crisis compounds existing challenges for Australian farmers,
who are already struggling with shortages of fuel and
fertilizer due to the Iran war. Industry estimates suggest
Western Australia's grain harvest could fall ~45% from a
record 27 Mt last season to around 15 Mt on insuﬃcient
fertilizer applications.
Trading Commentary
Cape
A backwards step for Cape paper, closing well in the red for
the day and backed by a negative physical index print of
-$368, a break in the recent run of positive prints. May
started the day trading just oﬀ last night closing levels, and a
series of better oﬀers left the contract closing at $33400,
with lows of $33250. Jun traded $33200 down to $32750,
closing just oﬀ the lows at $33800. Q3 traded $30750 down
to lows of $30500, valued at $30400 at close. Q4 traded a few
times between $30400-$30300. Cal27 traded $25650 and
closed at $25550, with lows of $25500.
PMX
Pmx traded ﬂat across the whole curve in today session, may
was paid at a high of 19350 and a low of 19100 closing at
19200, jun traded at a low of 19450 up to 19700 causing the
jun/jul to get paid at 375. Q3 held steady bouncing around
18600 to 18800. Q4 saw participation today printing 17175 -
17250, cal 27 saw a narrow range of 14800 - 14850. Overall
the pmx curve remained ﬂat into the close.
SMX + HANDY
SMX marked was relatively ﬂat to yesterday, trading within a
similar range over the day, with liquidity largely focused to
the prompt months. May traded between 18100 – 18500 and
Jun 17950 – 18300 in over 2500 lots, accounting for the
majority of the days cleared volume. Q3 traded within a tight
range 16900 – 17000, Q4 15650 – 15800 and Cal27 traded
13200. The Handy market once again was supported, Jun
trading 16200, Jul 15250, Q3 at 14800 and Q3+Q4 at 14400.Cape 180 5TC

items.parsed_text: 23rd April 2026 Iron Ore TSI 62%: 107.60 -0.40 TSI Premium Coking Coal: - - Brent UK Oil: 102.88 0.97 EUA: 73.47 0.40 BDI 2,673 -2 BCI 180 4,315 -41 BPI 1,965 -6 BSI 1,522 38 BHSI 791 10 Market Fundamentals West Australian Grain Under Pressure A surging mouse plague in Western Australia, which accounts for around half of all Australian grain exports, threatens the 2025/26 growing season, newswires report. With as many 3000-4000 burrows per hectare in West Australia,farmers are fearing a full-scale plague as numbers also continue to rise in the Southern part of the country. Historically, rodents can impact yields by 5–15% in affected zones, especially during the April-May planting window. This crisis compounds existing challenges for Australian farmers, who are already struggling with shortages of fuel and fertilizer due to the Iran war. Industry estimates suggest Western Australia's grain harvest could fall ~45% from a record 27 Mt last season to around 15 Mt on insuﬃcient fertilizer applications. Trading Commentary Cape A backwards step for Cape paper, closing well in the red for the day and backed by a negative physical index print of -$368, a break in the recent run of positive prints. May started the day trading just off last night closing levels, and a series of better offers left the contract closing at $33400, with lows of $33250. Jun traded $33200 down to $32750, closing just off the lows at $33800. Q3 traded $30750 down to lows of $30500, valued at $30400 at close. Q4 traded a few times between $30400-$30300. Cal27 traded $25650 and closed at $25550, with lows of $25500. Q3 traded within a tight range 16900 – 17000, Q4 15650 – 15800 and Cal27 traded 13200.
